correctness.rationale: A shuffle is a nondecreasing gap vector g with bits given by g_i<j. Repeated rows or columns and inversely ordered pairs force an implication between query bits. On an increasing support, choices j−1 or j for selected g_i realize all patterns unrestricted. Each trace fiber is the linear-extension set of the chains plus the oriented queried edges. If it is not a singleton, a connected graph of adjacent incomparable swaps contains an edge and hence both signs. A word has no admissible swap exactly when all its unlike-letter adjacencies are queried. On a diagonal the successive unlike-letter switches must use equal indices 1,2,…; the first run has length one and each internal run length two. For a<b the final run must be B, so the start is determined by a mod 2, and the only potentially obstructing word is even (even B-runs before A, except for the initial one-letter B-run only when a is even). Reversal with exchange of chains preserves B-before-A inversions. In the balanced case both starts are possible and they give inversion parities 0 and m mod 2. For the truncated diagonal, the letter immediately following the first of A_m and B_m is of the other chain, giving an unqueried adjacency. The empty support and m=1 are included. The replay independently reproduced all three stated balanced polynomials from direct even traces.
residual_risks: Independent replay covered only (3,3), (4,4), and (5,5), not all profiles. The all-parameter conclusion follows from the proof, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: This is an all-parameter classification of a natural sign-restricted comparison class. It explains why every non-singleton trace fiber is harmless and identifies exactly when a maximal support fails even though the unrestricted dimension and global parity counts may look benign. The loss for balanced odd chains is a structural boundary, not just a finite count.
residual_risks: The criterion does not assert an efficient decision algorithm or a closed all-profile face polynomial.
